title: Python interview idioms
note: Imports are allowed. Put these at the top of the sheet; they remove most of the boilerplate.
code:
from collections import deque, Counter, defaultdict
from heapq import heappush, heappop, heapify
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right
from functools import lru_cache

queue = deque([1, 2, 3])
queue.append(4)          # push right
queue.popleft()          # pop left, O(1)

heap = []                # min-heap
heappush(heap, 5)
heappop(heap)
max_heap = []            # negate values
heappush(max_heap, -x)

bisect_left(a, x)        # first index with a[i] >= x
bisect_right(a, x)       # first index with a[i] > x

counts = Counter("aab")  # {"a": 2, "b": 1}
groups = defaultdict(list)
groups[key].append(value)

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def solve(state):
    ...

title: Complexity & input sizes
note: Choose the target complexity before coding. If your plan is slower than the budget, change the plan.

title: Two pointers (sorted pair sum)
note: Move the pointer that can still improve the sum. Skip duplicates when you need unique pairs.

title: Sliding window (variable size)
note: Expand right, shrink left while invalid, update the answer while valid. Each index enters and leaves once.
code:
left = 0
state = {}  # counts, sum, ...
for right, x in enumerate(a):
    add(state, x)
    while not valid(state):
        remove(state, a[left])
        left += 1
    best = max(best, right - left + 1)
return best

title: Binary search (lower bound)
note: Invariant: the answer stays in [lo, hi]. hi starts at n so the answer may be n.

title: Monotonic stack (next greater)
note: Each index is pushed and popped at most once. Store indices, not values, when you need distances.

title: BFS on a grid
note: Mark visited when enqueueing, not when popping, otherwise the queue explodes with duplicates.

title: Backtracking
note: Append a copy of the path, never the path itself. Prune as early as possible; with a sorted input you can break.

title: Heap: k largest / running median
note: heapq is a min-heap; push -x for a max-heap. Two heaps for the median: max-heap for the small half, min-heap for the large half.
code:
import heapq

# k largest: keep a min-heap of size k
for x in stream:
    heapq.heappush(h, x)
    if len(h) > k:
        heapq.heappop(h)
# h[0] is the k-th largest

# max-heap
heapq.heappush(maxh, -x)
largest = -maxh[0]

title: Graph traversal & cycles
note: Use a visited set for components; use three colours for directed cycles. For an undirected cycle, track the parent or use Union-Find.

title: Dijkstra
note: Only for non-negative weights. Skip stale heap entries with d > dist[u].

title: Bellman-Ford with K stops
note: One round = one more flight. Relax from a copy of the previous round; relaxing in place allows too many edges.

title: Topological sort (Kahn)
note: Process nodes with indegree 0. If fewer than n nodes come out, there is a cycle.

title: Union-Find
note: Path compression plus union by size. Count components as n - successful unions.

title: Minimum spanning tree
note: Prim is easier on dense graphs (no edge list). Kruskal sorts edges and uses Union-Find; it needs O(E) memory.

title: DP 1-D rolling
note: Write the recurrence, then keep only the states it reads.
code:
# House Robber
two_back = one_back = 0
for x in nums:
    two_back, one_back = one_back, max(one_back, two_back + x)
return one_back

title: DP 2-D (LCS / edit distance)
note: Two rows are enough. Row 0 is the empty prefix of one string.

title: 0/1 Knapsack (1-D)
note: Capacity loop must go DOWN, so dp[c - w] still belongs to the previous item.

title: LIS (patience sorting)
note: tails[k] is the smallest tail of an increasing subsequence of length k + 1. tails is not the subsequence itself.

title: DP patterns: coins, intervals, bitmask
note: Name the state before coding. Coin change is unbounded; intervals iterate by length; bitmask DP needs n <= 20.

title: Linked list
note: A dummy node removes the empty-list special case. Middle uses fast/slow; reverse uses prev/cur/nxt.

title: Tree traversals & BST
note: Inorder of a BST is sorted. Level order captures len(q) before the inner loop. BST validation passes (low, high) bounds.

title: Trie
note: Children dict plus an end flag. A prefix existing is not the same as a word existing.

title: Design
note: LRU: hash map + doubly linked list (or OrderedDict). Min Stack: parallel mins. Queue from two stacks: pour only when the outbox is empty.

title: Matrix: spiral, rotate, zeroes
note: Spiral uses four walls. Rotate is transpose + reverse rows; matrix[:] keeps the same object. Zeroes uses the first row/column as markers.

title: Bit manipulation
note: XOR cancels pairs. n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit; use it for bit counting and powers of two.
code:
x ^ x                 # 0
x ^ 0                 # x
x & (x - 1)           # clear the lowest set bit
x & -x                # isolate the lowest set bit
x | (1 << k)          # set bit k
x & ~(1 << k)         # clear bit k
(x >> k) & 1          # test bit k

# every subset of mask
sub = mask
while sub:
    ...
    sub = (sub - 1) & mask

title: Math: gcd, sieve, fast power
tag: O(log n) / O(n log log n)
note: Use math.gcd; write the sieve once. Binary exponentiation handles negative exponents by inverting the base.

title: Strings: KMP, rolling hash
note: The prefix table says how far to jump on a mismatch. Rolling hash gives O(1) window updates for multiple patterns.

title: Interview checklist
note: Say the plan out loud. Silent coding is the most common failure; the interviewer scores the reasoning, not only the code.
table: size, duplicates, negatives, empty, return type

title: Pattern triggers
note: Read the constraints first, then the shape of the input. The pattern usually announces itself in the first two sentences.
